_comment: What setup installs, as data. The code implements one function per component named here, in this order; tests/test_vocab.py holds the two equal, both directions. Templates are relative to this file's folder. Nothing here may name a repo, a repo path or a repo command (./dev.sh audit content).

components.name: repo
components.installs: for a path that does not exist (or an empty folder whose parent is not in a work tree): the folder and git init

components.name: rules
components.installs: the shared-rules block of CLAUDE.md, between markers; the repo's own sections untouched
components.head: templates/CLAUDE.md

components.name: hooks
components.installs: every file the hooks dependency lists (dependencies.json: its `list --json` over its source; --hooks-from DIR overrides the source): each shared hook and its test in .claude/hooks/, and the shared libraries in the destination the listing gives. Absent: installed; equal by meaning (the dependency's one comparator: comments and blank lines aside) but not byte for byte: rewritten from the source, "header refreshed"; logic differs: drift, never overwritten without --rebuild (no --node), which overwrites it from the source when it is in the rebuild scope (and refuses, writing nothing, while a copy it renders there has changes git does not hold, unless --overwrite-uncommitted); one line per file that differed (`rebuild` below). Without the dependency (a lone clone): only --hooks-from DIR, its hooks folder, byte for byte. Plus .claude/settings.proposed.json for Jacob when settings.json lacks a registration (in a repo setup is creating, that same render is written as .claude/settings.json itself and committed, with no proposal: PLAN-repo-setup §7.9; an existing repo's settings.json is never touched), including (with --plugins FILE) each plug-in hook the registry says applies here: run in place, never copied; with --user-scope FILE (the hook copies report), a shared hook the user settings already run is neither copied nor registered per repo in the proposal ("covered by user scope: <files>"; an existing copy is kept, an existing per-repo registration left out of the proposal so it does not run twice); unknown coverage is never covered

rebuild._comment: --rebuild without --node (PLAN-repo-setup §7.12, Jacob's yes of 2026-10-05): a file the hooks listing renders into a folder directly under `scope_root` (the listing's destinations: the hooks folder and the libraries' folder) is overwritten from the source whatever it differs in; nothing else ever is (settings.json and settings.proposed.json sit in scope_root itself, not in a folder under it; .githooks/; anything setup does not render). Every hook file that differed gets one line {path, kind, action, detail}, in any run; tests/test_rebuild.py holds kinds and actions equal to what core.py emits, both ways.

kinds.header-only: equal by meaning (the dependency's comparator: comments and blank lines aside), not byte for byte
kinds.logic: differs by meaning: the copy's logic is not the source's
kinds.bytes: differs byte for byte with no comparator by meaning (no hooks dependency): header or logic, not told
kinds.mode: byte-equal, but not executable where the source is

actions.refreshed: rewritten from the source: by construction no logic changed (every run)
actions.rewritten: overwritten from the source (--rebuild only, in scope only)
actions.kept: left byte-unchanged: drift (no --rebuild, or outside the scope)
actions.failed: the write was tried and did not work; the reason is the detail

components.name: todo
components.installs: TODO.md with the four standard headings, if absent

components.name: check
components.installs: a ./dev.sh stub that FAILS with 'not implemented: fill in the contract' (with --json: the one check schema's red report, check `stub-unfilled`), if absent; never fakes green

components.name: services
components.installs: services.json, if absent (PLAN-routing-tree.md §14.8): the skeleton, the repo's name and its `check` entry only (the check stub's command); the owner adds `write` entries and tags. An existing one is the owner's, never touched; the shared `services-valid` gates it

components.name: cli
components.installs: nothing: cli.json ({store, cli, verbs}) is the owner's to write when the repo has a store. No skeleton passes its schema (a store and an executable cli are required), and a repo with no store needs none; the shared `accessor` gates both

components.name: data
components.installs: the store, generated (PLAN-repo-setup.md §7.11): when cli.json declares the import and verify verbs and no path its `store` names is on disk, `<cli> import` then `<cli> verify --json`, run in the repo with DATA_REPO (the data repo's root: --data-repo, else the environment) passed through; installed only when the store is on disk after and every item verify reports is `same`. An existing store is never dropped (part of one present is needs-owner); DATA_REPO unset, or not a folder, is needs-jacob; never in a dry run; the store is not committed

components.name: params
components.installs: checks.json, if absent: the baseline, no parameter set, so every shared check runs at its defaults where it says it applies. An existing one is the owner's

baseline._comment: Parameters for the shared checks: {"<check>": {"<param>": value}}. None set: every check at its defaults. Keys starting with _ are comments.

components.name: ignore
components.installs: .gitignore with the baseline entries if absent; in an existing one, only the entries git does not already ignore, appended (nothing rewritten or reordered); a negation of one is drift, as is an append that would re-ignore what a root negation keeps (git decides, in a scratch repo; a negation with a pattern in it cannot be tested and blocks the append); a committed file a baseline line covers is drift, never untracked
components.header: # Baseline from the setup tool: its settings proposal, local env files, backups, the shared hooks' run state. Add your own lines anywhere; setup only appends what is missing.
components._entries: line: what is written; probe: a path that line must make git ignore. Present means git ignores the probe through the repo's own ignore files (by meaning, not bytes).

components.name: githooks
components.installs: the git-side gates (PLAN-hard-gates.md §2, §3 rows 3 and 6, §7 phase 2, §7a): .githooks/commit-msg (refuses a commit made in a Claude Code session without an `Agent:` trailer, or with `Agent: jacob`; writes `Agent: jacob` on one made outside a session; writes `check: full | resumed from K/N | none`), .githooks/pre-commit (refuses unless the staged tree is the one the check passed on, and the shared checks' no-secrets is ok) and .githooks/check-pass (the one recorder and matcher of a pass), each if absent; a changed one is drift, never overwritten. core.hooksPath is set only once nothing would be refused for want of wiring: the check records its pass (`record` below, in the check file: a text probe), a checks CLI is configured (--checks, kept in this clone's git config `config` below, never a tracked file), the `stamp` hook is registered, no other hook folder is in use; never in a repo setup is creating (its check is the stub). Another core.hooksPath is drift, never overridden. When core.hooksPath already names the folder, a hook git runs (`runs` below) is withheld, not written, while any of those conditions is unmet: written, it would refuse every commit, setup's own output among them (needs-jacob when the stamp is unregistered, else needs-owner, with the reasons). needs-jacob until settings.json (or user scope) runs both hooks the list below names
components._runs: the files git itself runs by name (a hook): check-pass is called by them and by the check, never by git

components.name: commit
components.installs: in a repo setup just created only: one commit of exactly the files it wrote, .claude/settings.json among them (never add -A, never the settings proposal)

components.name: remote
components.installs: with --github only: a GitHub repo (public by default, --private on request), origin, and a push of the current branch; verified by the pushed sha and the visibility

components.name: agent
components.installs: nothing: a folder agent is a roster entry, which setup does not own

components.name: server
components.installs: nothing: the group-server entry has no defined shape yet (group servers are not built)

components.name: node
components.installs: with --node only (PLAN-repo-setup §7.5, §7.10): each child node.json lists, set up in turn, created as a repo nested in this one when absent, a child with its own node.json recursing, never with --github; with --rebuild, every file node.json lists as generated, rendered again in place (the setup pass is then a dry run), one line per file (rebuild_statuses); never a record, never a generated file with uncommitted changes
components._render: the components a --rebuild renders afresh, as a new repo in a throwaway folder, for the node's path and name

components.name: registry
components.installs: in a node run only, once its children are set up: registry.proposed.json, the union of the node's and each child's services.json keyed by path (`.` for the node), for Jacob to apply to the registry node.json names (as the settings proposal); nothing when it already equals that union. Only the registry's `services` is rendered: its roles and owners have no defined shape here

components.name: gates
components.installs: nothing: with --checks CLI only, and last, once everything is rendered (never in a dry run or a rebuild): `CLI list`, then `CLI run <path>`, then `CLI one <gate> <path>` for each contract gate below that `run` left out (one that applies only under a role, as the audit's), in sequence; their results are this line (a fail is drift, an error or a fault failed, unchecked named). A contract gate not in the list, or reporting nothing, fails the line by name: unchecked, never a pass
components._contract: PLAN-routing-tree.md §14.8: the shared checks beside the contract files

rebuild_statuses.regenerated: a generated file rendered byte for byte, mode included, as the tree holds it (or, absent there, as the last commit does: written back)
rebuild_statuses.drift: a generated file rendered otherwise, or in neither the tree nor the last commit: the render is written and git diff is the finding; one with uncommitted changes is kept, not rendered
rebuild_statuses.record: a file node.json lists as content (or node.json itself): never written
rebuild_statuses.unaccounted: in the tree (tracked, or untracked and not ignored), not under a child, named by neither list
rebuild_statuses.failed: the setup render failed, or setup renders no such file; nothing written for it

statuses.installed: setup wrote it (or, in --dry-run, would write it)
statuses.unchanged: already as setup would make it; nothing written
statuses.drift: differs from what setup would make; reported, not overwritten
statuses.needs-jacob: a proposal was written for Jacob to apply (settings stay his)
statuses.needs-harness: outside setup's lane; the line to add is printed
statuses.needs-owner: installed, but the repo's owner must fill it in
statuses.none: nothing to do: an opt-in step not requested, or a step that does not apply to this repo
statuses.failed: setup tried and it did not work; the reason is printed
